desc: Ideation: DP state = (alternating sum, parity of subsequence length, product capped at limit+1); zero multiplication resets product to 0 even from overflow; dict-of-sets keeps state space small since nums[i] ≤ 12 and limit ≤ 5000.
Implement DP as two dicts (parity 0/1): dict mapping sum -> set of products, non-empty subsequences only (no virtual seed).

Transition per element x: snapshot dicts (skip), then for each state add take-transition with ns = s+x (parity 0) or s-x (parity 1), np = 0 if x==0 else min(p*x, limit+1); also allow x to start a fresh subsequence.
Final scan: max product ≤ limit over both parity dicts at sum k; return -1 if none.

Clean up the empty-subsequence guard: removed virtual seed; non-emptiness guaranteed structurally (states created only by starting a subsequence with a single element, extensions only append to existing non-empty states).

Test against the three given examples plus edge cases: zeros in nums, |k| > sum(nums), single element, all products > limit, product 0 as only valid answer, k=0 with product 1 (nums=[1] → -1; nums=[1,1] → 1). All verified.
